primaryEvidence.article: A New Technique for Computed-Tomography Urethrography in Males: The Clamp Method
primaryEvidence.reviewed: Author-institution PDF of the original paper: methods, cohort/results and discussion limitations, particularly page 9. Publisher endpoint rate-limited during this review; no paywall bypass.
primaryEvidence.supports: Selected 22-man urethral-disease cohort; dedicated contrast-filled lumen assessment; authors did not measure spongiofibrosis thickness on CT because of similar attenuation of scar and adjacent erectile tissue.
primaryEvidence.doesNotSupport: Routine normal-population tissue visibility, a whole spongiosal CT boundary, validated patient-space mapping, universal CT diagnostic performance or any procedural recommendation.
primaryEvidence.sourceRights: Paper declares CC BY 4.0. Only an original concise factual paraphrase and citation are proposed; no PDF, figure, table, patient data or protocol reproduced.

primaryEvidence.supports: Corpus spongiosum surrounds the urethra; paired corpora cavernosa are separate erectile columns.
